items.fact: Reason for call: Father's pain is up; son wants to increase the pain medicine (Hospice patient with bone pain)
Symptom present: pain, 5/10, hips and lower back, worse over the last 3 days
Medication: meth a dome, 10 mg, three times a day, status: taking
Pertinent negative: vomiting
Symptom present: sleeping more, sleeps most of the day
Pertinent negative: constipation, Last bowel movement yesterday morning and normal
Symptom present: decreased appetite, a few bites at each meal
Background: Wants to double the dose because the pain is worse
Nurse action (planned): message to team, hospice physician, because pain review and dose request
Nurse action (planned): callback, tomorrow morning
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, because do not change the dose until the physician reviews
Instruction given (medication administration): Give exactly as labeled, write each dose and time on a log, and never double up
Instruction given (return precautions): Call if he is very sleepy, hard to wake, or breathing slowly; 911 if he cannot be woken, when: very sleepy; hard to wake; slow breathing
Instruction given (comfort measures): Pillows to support the hips, repositioning every 2 hours, and a warm pack on low
Reason for call: Requested nebulizer supplies for her daughter (Pediatric home care patient who uses a nebulizer)
Supply: neb vials, 6 vials remaining
Supply: child nebulizer mask, 1 cracked mask masks remaining
Supply: nebulizer tubing, 1 sets remaining
Symptom present: cough with a cold, mild
Pertinent negative: wheezing or fast breathing now
Nurse action (planned): supply order, neb vials, child masks and tubing
Nurse action (planned): delivery coordination, tomorrow
Instruction given (equipment use): Rinse the cup and mask with warm soapy water after every treatment, air dry them, and never use a cracked mask

Instruction given (return precautions): Call for fast or hard breathing, a treatment that does not help, or a fever of one hundred two, and dial 911 for blue lips, when: fast breathing; treatment not helping; fever 102; blue lips
Reason for call: Reported that her father-in-law fell and hit his head while on a blood thinner (Home health patient on warfarin)
Symptom present: fall with head strike, severe
Symptom present: bleeding cut above the ear, moderate
Symptom present: new headache
Symptom present: repeating himself
Medication: warfarin, 5 mg, once a day in the evening, status: taking, last dose: last night
Pertinent negative: vomiting or loss of consciousness
Nurse action (advised): escalation 911 ed, 911
Nurse action (planned): on call page, on-call clinician
Instruction given (emergency instructions): Call 911 now, keep him still and lying down, press a clean cloth firmly on the cut, and give nothing by mouth
Instruction given (medication administration): Do not give any more of his blood thinner and tell the paramedics he takes warfarin
Reason for call: Resident's pain and intake seem worse but the reports are inconsistent (Resident at Cedar Crest Care Center)
Symptom present: pain, 3 to 6 out of 10, left hip
Symptom present: decreased intake, a quarter to half of meals
Medication: oxycodone, 5 mg, every 4 hours, as needed, status: prescribed
Pertinent negative: fever
Pertinent negative: falls
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, oxycodone, because give if pain is above 4 and it has been at least 4 hours
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, tomorrow morning, because assess pain and intake
Nurse action (planned): callback, tomorrow after the visit
Instruction given (symptom monitoring): Record a pain score and facial expression every 4 hours, and a meal percentage after each meal
Instruction given (comfort measures): Pillow between the knees, reposition every 2 hours, and offer favorite foods
Instruction given (return precautions): Call for pain above 7, very sleepy, fever, or a fall, when: pain above 7; very sleepy; fever; fall
Reason for call: Asked about her brother's new pain medicine instructions after he took ibuprofen (Home health patient with liver disease)
Medication: ibuprofen, 200 mg, as needed, as needed, status: stopped, last dose: two tablets this morning
Medication: acetaminophen, 500 mg, as needed, as needed, status: prescribed, last dose: none yet
Symptom present: upset stomach, mild
Pertinent negative: black stools or vomiting blood
Nurse action (planned): message to team, clinician, because ibuprofen taken in a patient with liver disease
Nurse action (planned): callback, tomorrow

Instruction given (medication administration): Take no more ibuprofen or similar pain pills, use acetaminophen only up to four of the five hundred milligram tablets in a day, and check cold medicines for hidden acetaminophen

Instruction given (return precautions): Call right away or dial 911 for black or bloody stools, vomiting blood, severe belly pain or yellowing skin, when: black stools; vomiting blood; severe belly pain; yellow skin
Reason for call: Cough and runny nose for two days
Symptom present: cough, mild and dry, 2 days
Symptom present: runny nose
Pertinent negative: fever
Pertinent negative: shortness of breath
Nurse action (planned): callback, tomorrow
Instruction given (comfort measures): Warm fluids and a spoon of honey, humidifier at night, rest
Instruction given (return precautions): Call for fever of 100.4 or higher, trouble breathing, or a cough lasting past a week, when: fever 100.4+; trouble breathing; cough over a week
Reason for call: Father is severely agitated and not settling despite medicine (Hospice patient with an indwelling urinary catheter)
Symptom present: agitation, severe, past two hours
Medication: lorazepam, 1 mg, as needed, status: taking
Background: Has a urinary catheter in place
Pertinent negative: signs of pain
Nurse action (completed): on call page, on-call physician, because agitation not responding to lorazepam
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, lorazepam, because no more doses until the physician gives orders
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, within 45 minutes
Instruction given (safety): Stay with him, keep the bed low, and gently keep his hands away from the catheter
Instruction given (comfort measures): Dim the lights, speak slowly and calmly, and reduce noise
Instruction given (return precautions): Call right away if he falls, becomes combative, or is hard to wake, when: fall; combative; hard to wake
Reason for call: Pain and a question about when she can give the next dose (Hospice patient at home)
Symptom present: pain, 5/10, hips
Medication: dilaudin, 2 mg, as needed, status: taking
Pertinent negative: vomiting
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, dilaudin, next dose at least 4 hours after the last
Nurse action (planned): callback, in an hour
Instruction given (comfort measures): Reposition with pillows, warm pack on the hips on low, and calm music
Instruction given (return precautions): Call if pain rises above 7, she is hard to wake, or her breathing slows, when: pain above 7; hard to wake; slow breathing
Reason for call: Reported a four pound weight gain and ankle swelling with heart failure (Home health patient with heart failure)
Measurement: weight 214 lb
Symptom present: ankle swelling, mild
Symptom present: winded on the stairs, mild
Medication: furosemide, 40 mg, every morning, status: taking, last dose: this morning
Pertinent negative: chest pain or shortness of breath at rest
Nurse action (planned): message to team, clinician, because weight gain with swelling
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, tomorrow
Instruction given (symptom monitoring): Weigh every morning after using the bathroom and write it down, and call for a gain of more than two pounds in a day or five in a week
Instruction given (hydration nutrition): Keep salt low, skip pizza and canned soup, and keep fluids to the amount the doctor set
Instruction given (emergency instructions): Call 911 for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or fainting, when: chest pain; severe shortness of breath; fainting
Reason for call: Mother may have taken two days of pills at once and is confused (Mother manages her own weekly pillbox)
Background: The Tuesday and Wednesday compartments of the pillbox were both empty this morning; the caller thinks her mother took both days' pills around 8
Medication: metoprolol, 25 mg, once a day, status: extra_dose
Medication: furosemide, 20 mg, once a day, status: extra_dose
Medication: amlodipine, 5 mg, once a day, status: extra_dose
Symptom present: confusion and sleepiness, asking the same questions and drifting off, since about 10 this morning
Measurement: blood pressure 98/58
Measurement: pulse 54
Pertinent negative: fainting or chest pain
Nurse action (completed): on call page, on-call physician, because possible double dose of blood pressure medicines
Nurse action (planned): pharmacy contact, poison control
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, within 2 hours
Nurse action (planned): callback, in 10 minutes
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, metoprolol, because no more pills today until the physician advises
Instruction given (safety): Have her lie down or sit, stand slowly, and do not leave her alone
Instruction given (symptom monitoring): Check pulse and blood pressure every 15 minutes and write them down

Instruction given (emergency instructions): Call 911 for fainting, chest pain, trouble breathing, a pulse under 50, or if she cannot be woken, when: fainting; chest pain; trouble breathing; pulse under 50; cannot be woken
Instruction given (medication administration): Switch to a pillbox that has all pills for one day in a single compartment and keep a log
Reason for call: Wanted to check his father's medicines after a hospital stay and reported giving both blood thinners one evening (Recently discharged home health patient with atrial fibrillation)
Medication: apixaban, 5 mg, twice a day, status: taking, last dose: this morning
Medication: warfarin, 3 mg, once a day, status: extra_dose, last dose: Saturday evening, given along with the apixaban
Medication: metoprolol succinate, 50 mg, once a day, status: taking, last dose: this morning
Medication: furosemide, 20 mg, once a day, status: taking, last dose: this morning
Medication: atorvastatin, 40 mg, at night, status: taking, last dose: last night
Pertinent negative: bleeding or unusual bruising
Background: Warfarin was replaced by apixaban at discharge and the old warfarin bottle is still in the house
Nurse action (planned): on call page, on-call clinician, because both blood thinners given on Saturday evening
Nurse action (planned): pharmacy contact, dispensing pharmacy, because confirm the discharge medicine list
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, tomorrow
Instruction given (medication administration): Give no more warfarin, put the old bottle in a bag away from the others, and give the new blood thinner twelve hours apart

Instruction given (return precautions): Call right away or dial 911 for bleeding that will not stop, black or bloody stools, vomiting blood, a bad headache, or a fall with a head injury, when: uncontrolled bleeding; black or bloody stools; vomiting blood; severe headache; head injury
Instruction given (safety): Use a soft toothbrush and electric razor, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, and use a pill organizer filled from the current list
Reason for call: Reported that her father cannot stop vomiting and cannot keep down medicine (Hospice patient on an anti-nausea medicine)
Symptom present: vomiting, severe
Medication: ondansetron, 4 mg, every eight hours as needed, as needed, status: taking, last dose: two doses today, both vomited back up
Symptom present: weakness and dry mouth
Pertinent negative: pain or blood in the vomit
Nurse action (planned): on call page, on-call clinician, because vomiting not controlled and unable to keep down medicine
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, within two hours
Instruction given (comfort measures): Nothing by mouth for an hour, then ice chips or tiny sips, keep his head raised, and moisten his mouth with a swab
Instruction given (medication administration): Do not give any more of the dissolving tablet until the clinician calls with another way to give it
Reason for call: Reported a sudden severe headache with vision change (Home health patient recovering from surgery)
Symptom present: sudden severe headache, 9/10, about 40 minutes ago
Symptom present: blurred vision in the right eye
Symptom present: vomiting, once
Nurse action (advised): escalation 911 ed, because sudden severe headache with vision change
Instruction given (emergency instructions): Call 911 now, do not drive, unlock the front door, sit down, and take no more pills
Reason for call: Asked for a sleeping pill for his mother who has not slept for three nights (Home health patient with trouble sleeping)
Medication: zolpidem, 5 mg, at bedtime, status: requested, last dose: none
Symptom present: poor sleep and night wandering, moderate
Pertinent negative: fall or pain
Background: She has tried melatonin and a warm bath without relief
Nurse action (planned): message to team, her doctor, because request for a sleep medicine
Nurse action (planned): callback, tomorrow afternoon
Instruction given (comfort measures): Keep a regular bedtime, avoid caffeine and long naps, dim the lights, and try a warm drink before bed
Instruction given (safety): Put a night light in the hall and bathroom, clear the path, and lock the outside doors at night
Reason for call: Skin tear on his forearm (Fragile skin; bumped his arm on a door frame)
Symptom present: skin tear, about an inch long, right forearm, this morning
Symptom present: bleeding, bled a little and stopped after 10 minutes of pressure
Pertinent negative: ongoing bleeding
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, tomorrow morning, because dress the skin tear
Instruction given (skin care): Leave it covered with a non-stick pad and gauze wrap, do not use tape on the skin, keep it dry
Instruction given (return precautions): Call for bleeding that restarts, redness, warmth, pus, or fever; press firmly for 10 minutes if it bleeds, when: bleeding restarts; redness; warmth; pus; fever
Reason for call: Requested dressing supplies for her client's pressure sore (Home health patient with a pressure sore on the tailbone)
Supply: foam dressings, 4 dressings remaining
Supply: wound wash, 1 bottles remaining
Supply: disposable gloves, none remaining (boxes)
Symptom present: more drainage than usual on the dressing, mild
Pertinent negative: odor or fever
Nurse action (planned): supply order, foam dressings, wound wash and gloves
Nurse action (planned): delivery coordination, this evening
Nurse action (planned): message to team, wound care nurse, because increased drainage from the tailbone sore
Instruction given (skin care): Turn him every two hours, keep pressure off the tailbone with pillows, and keep the dressing clean and dry

Instruction given (return precautions): Call for a bad smell, fever, spreading redness, much more drainage, or the wound getting larger or darker, when: smell; fever; spreading redness; heavy drainage; larger or darker wound
Reason for call: Wanted to know whether his wife's morning dizziness and blood pressure are a concern (Home health patient on a blood pressure medicine)
Symptom present: dizziness, mild
Medication: lisinopril, 10 mg, once a day, status: taking, last dose: this morning
Pertinent negative: headache
Measurement: blood pressure 134/82
Pertinent negative: chest pain or fall
Nurse action (planned): callback, this afternoon
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, tomorrow
Instruction given (safety): Stand up slowly, sit on the edge of the bed first, use the walker or hold a steady surface, and sit down at once if lightheaded
Instruction given (return precautions): Call for fainting, chest pain, a severe headache or if the dizziness gets worse, when: fainting; chest pain; severe headache; worsening dizziness
Reason for call: Reported that her husband said he did not want to be here anymore and could take all his pills (Hospice patient with metastatic colon cancer)
Symptom present: statement of not wanting to be here and taking all his pills
Symptom present: abdominal pain, moderate
Pertinent negative: has taken extra pills
Background: She moved the pill bottles to the kitchen and he is awake and calm now
Nurse action (planned): on call page, on-call clinician, because patient statement about taking all his pills
Nurse action (planned): social work referral, hospice social worker
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, within the hour
Instruction given (safety): Stay with him, keep all medicines locked up or out of reach, and give each dose herself
Instruction given (crisis resources): Call or text 988 anytime, and call 911 if he tries to take pills or hurt himself, when: tries to take pills; tries to hurt himself
Reason for call: Needs glucose test strips and lancets (Patient checks her sugar twice a day)
Supply: glucose test strips, 10 strips remaining
Supply: lancets, none remaining (lancets)
Measurement: fasting blood sugar 132
Nurse action (planned): supply order, test strips and lancets, delivery in 2 days
Instruction given (symptom monitoring): Check once a day in the morning until the new supplies arrive and write the numbers down
Instruction given (return precautions): Call if sugar is over 300 or under 70, or if she is confused, very thirsty, or shaky, when: sugar over 300; sugar under 70; confusion; thirst; shaky
Reason for call: Found a woman sitting on her kitchen floor unable to get up (Home care client who lives alone and receives volunteer grocery deliveries)
Symptom present: found on the floor and unable to get up
Symptom absent: pain or injury
Symptom present: unknown whether she fell or slid down
Pertinent negative: hitting her head or losing consciousness
Nurse action (planned): on call page, on-call clinician
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, within two hours
Instruction given (safety): Do not lift her alone, keep her warm with a blanket and a cushion, and stay with her until the nurse arrives

Instruction given (emergency instructions): Call 911 if she has pain, cannot move a leg, becomes confused or hard to wake, or has trouble breathing, when: pain; cannot move a leg; confusion; trouble breathing
Reason for call: Wife is agitated and he wants to know whether he can give another haloperidol dose (Hospice patient with night-time agitation)
Symptom present: agitation, pulling at the blanket and trying to get out of bed
Medication: haloperidol, 0.5 mg, as needed, status: taking
Pertinent negative: signs of pain
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, haloperidol, wait until 4 hours after the last dose
Nurse action (planned): callback, in 30 minutes
Instruction given (comfort measures): Dim the lights, speak calmly, play soft music, check for a full bladder, and sit with her
Instruction given (safety): Keep the bed rails or low bed and stay near so she does not fall
Instruction given (return precautions): Call if she becomes combative, cannot be calmed, or is very hard to wake, when: combative; cannot be calmed; hard to wake
Reason for call: Reported that his wife took twenty units of Lantus instead of ten and has a low sugar (Home health patient with type 1 diabetes)
Medication: Lantus, 20 units, once a day at bedtime, status: extra_dose, last dose: about forty minutes ago
Measurement: blood glucose 48
Symptom present: shakiness and sweating, moderate
Measurement: blood glucose recheck 92
Pertinent negative: passing out or seizure
Nurse action (planned): on call page, on-call clinician, because double dose of Lantus with low glucose
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, tomorrow morning
Instruction given (safety): Give half a cup of juice now, recheck in fifteen minutes, repeat if still under seventy, and stay with her tonight with a glucose check every two hours
Instruction given (emergency instructions): Call 911 if she cannot swallow, will not wake, or has a seizure, when: cannot swallow; will not wake; seizure
Reason for call: Reported that the dressing on his neighbor's shin wound came loose and is oozing (Home health patient with a shin wound; her daughter is out of town)
Symptom present: loose shin dressing with yellow oozing, mild
Symptom absent: fever or feeling warm
Pertinent negative: trouble eating or talking
Background: Her daughter is out of town until Sunday
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, tomorrow morning
Nurse action (planned): callback, her daughter
Instruction given (skin care): Cover the wound with clean dry gauze and tape, do not peel off any other dressing, and keep the leg propped up
Instruction given (return precautions): Call back or dial 911 if she gets a fever, confusion, red streaks up the leg, or heavy bleeding, when: fever; confusion; red streaks; heavy bleeding
Reason for call: Daughter is breathing fast with her ribs pulling in (5-year-old with a cold for three days)
Symptom present: fast breathing, breathing very fast, worse over the last hour
Symptom present: chest retractions, ribs pulling in with each breath
Measurement: temperature 102
Medication: acetaminophen, status: given during the call
Symptom present: sleepiness, very sleepy but wakes when called
Nurse action (advised): escalation 911 ed, now, because fast breathing with retractions and fever
Nurse action (planned): message to team, emergency department, because call ahead
Instruction given (emergency instructions): Call 911 now, keep her sitting upright, no food or drink, unlock the door
Instruction given (safety): Stay with her and keep her calm; do not drive her yourself if she gets worse or turns blue
Reason for call: Gave a routine update on her client after hip replacement and asked about showering (Two weeks after a hip replacement, home health patient)
Symptom present: hip pain, three out of ten
Background: He walks to the bathroom with a walker and eats three meals a day
Pertinent negative: incision redness or drainage
Measurement: temperature 98.4
Nurse action (planned): message to team, physical therapist, because confirm therapy schedule for this week
Instruction given (skin care): No shower until the surgeon clears it; sponge bathe and keep the incision dry and covered
Instruction given (safety): Keep the walker within reach, clear the path to the bathroom, and have him wear non-slip footwear
Instruction given (return precautions): Call for fever, spreading redness or drainage at the incision, or a calf that is swollen or painful
Reason for call: Gave her weekly check-in and asked about the stair exercises (Home health patient, age 92, who uses a walker)
Measurement: blood pressure 138/78
Symptom present: dull ache in the right knee, mild
Pertinent negative: dizziness or falls
Background: She walks with her walker and is enjoying her new hearing aids
Nurse action (completed): appointment scheduling, Wednesday
Instruction given (comfort measures): Do the stair exercises only as far as comfortable, rest between sets, and use a warm pack on the knee for fifteen minutes
Instruction given (callback invitation): Call any time if the knee swells, turns red, or she feels dizzy or falls
Reason for call: Requested colostomy supplies and reported skin redness around the stoma (Home health patient with a colostomy)
Supply: skin barrier wafers, 3 wafers remaining
Supply: stoma paste, none remaining (tubes)
Symptom present: redness around the stoma, mild
Pertinent negative: fever or pus at the stoma
Nurse action (planned): supply order, wafers, stoma paste and barrier powder
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, Tuesday
Instruction given (skin care): Change the pouch when it leaks, clean the skin with warm water only, dry it fully, and dust a little barrier powder before the wafer

Instruction given (return precautions): Call for fever, pus, a stoma that turns dark or purple, no output for a day with belly swelling or vomiting, when: fever; pus; dark stoma; no output with swelling
Reason for call: Asked how to give his mother's scheduled gabapentin and as-needed oxycodone together for leg pain (Home health patient with leg pain on a scheduled and an as-needed medicine)
Medication: gabapentin, 300 mg, three times daily, status: taking, last dose: at noon
Medication: oxycodone, 5 mg, every four hours as needed, as needed, status: taking, last dose: at two this afternoon
Symptom present: leg pain, five out of ten
Pertinent negative: excess sleepiness
Nurse action (planned): callback, tomorrow morning
Instruction given (medication administration): The gabapentin is scheduled three times a day regardless of pain, and the oxycodone is only as needed at least four hours apart
Instruction given (return precautions): Call if she is very sleepy, confused, or the pain stays high after oxycodone
Reason for call: Chest tightness and shortness of breath for 30 minutes (History of heart disease with a stent last year)
Symptom present: chest tightness, pressure in the center of the chest, 30 minutes
Symptom present: shortness of breath, 30 minutes
Symptom present: sweating, clammy
Background: Heart disease with a stent placed last year
Pertinent negative: fainting
Nurse action (advised): escalation 911 ed, now, because possible cardiac event
Nurse action (planned): message to team, emergency department, because give report ahead of arrival
Instruction given (emergency instructions): Call 911 now, have him sit and rest, unlock the front door, and gather his medication list
Instruction given (safety): Do not drive him yourself and stay with him
Reason for call: More secretions from his son's tracheostomy and low suction supplies (7-year-old with a tracheostomy)
Symptom present: increased tracheal secretions, clear and needing suction every 2 hours instead of every 4, past 2 days
Measurement: temperature 98.6
Pertinent negative: increased work of breathing, Color is normal and he is playing
Supply: suction catheters, 6 catheters remaining
Symptom present: mild cough, mild
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, tomorrow afternoon, because check secretions and humidification
Nurse action (planned): supply order, suction catheters, delivery tomorrow
Instruction given (symptom monitoring): Suction as needed when he sounds wet or coughs, and note the color and amount
Instruction given (comfort measures): Check that the humidifier or heated moisture exchanger is working and give extra fluids

Instruction given (return precautions): Call for yellow or green or bloody secretions, fever, or more work to breathe; 911 if he turns blue or the tube is blocked and cannot be cleared, when: yellow or green or bloody secretions; fever; work of breathing; blocked tube
Reason for call: Wife may have taken one of his metoprolol tablets by mistake (The two keep pill bottles next to each other)
Medication: metoprolol, 50 mg, 1 tablet, status: extra_dose
Symptom present: lightheadedness, mild
Measurement: pulse 62
Measurement: blood pressure 110/70
Pertinent negative: fainting, No chest pain or trouble breathing either
Pertinent negative: asthma or diabetes or heart rhythm problems
Medication: lisinopril, 10 mg, once a day, status: taking
Nurse action (completed): on call page, on-call physician, because possible accidental metoprolol ingestion
Nurse action (planned): callback, in 15 minutes
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, metoprolol, because no more of his tablets for her
Instruction given (safety): Have her lie down or sit, stand up slowly, and do not walk alone
Instruction given (symptom monitoring): Check pulse and blood pressure every 15 minutes and write them down
Instruction given (emergency instructions): Call 911 for fainting, chest pain, trouble breathing, or a pulse under 50, when: fainting; chest pain; trouble breathing; pulse under 50
Instruction given (medication administration): Keep each person's pills in a separate labeled organizer in different places
Reason for call: Asked which furosemide dose is correct because the bottle and the discharge paper disagree (Recently discharged home health patient with swollen ankles)
Medication: furosemide, 20 mg, once a day, status: taking, last dose: this morning
Background: The discharge paper lists furosemide forty milligrams once a day and the bottle label says twenty, so the correct dose is unresolved
Symptom present: swollen ankles, moderate
Pertinent negative: shortness of breath
Nurse action (planned): physician notification, discharging physician's office, because furosemide dose discrepancy between bottle and discharge paper
Nurse action (planned): callback, by end of day
Instruction given (medication administration): Give only the dose on the bottle label until the order is confirmed and keep the bottle and discharge paper together
Instruction given (return precautions): Call right away or dial 911 for trouble breathing, chest pain, or a sudden weight gain, when: trouble breathing; chest pain; sudden weight gain
Reason for call: Mother is up 2 pounds since yesterday (Heart failure patient who weighs herself daily)
Measurement: weight change up 2 pounds since yesterday
Pertinent negative: shortness of breath
Symptom present: ankle swelling, slight
Background: Ate soup and ham at a family dinner yesterday
Nurse action (planned): callback, tomorrow morning
Instruction given (hydration nutrition): Low-salt meals today, skip canned soup and deli meat, keep fluids as her doctor allows
Instruction given (symptom monitoring): Weigh every morning after using the bathroom, before eating, and write it down

Instruction given (return precautions): Call for a gain of 3 pounds in a day or 5 in a week, more swelling, or shortness of breath; 911 for severe trouble breathing, when: 3 pounds in a day; 5 in a week; swelling; shortness of breath
Reason for call: Asked what to do about her grandfather's missed morning steroid dose (Home health patient on a steroid)
Medication: predisone, 10 mg, every morning, status: missed, last dose: yesterday morning
Symptom present: restlessness and poor sleep, mild
Symptom present: increased appetite
Pertinent negative: stomach pain or black stools
Nurse action (planned): callback, tomorrow morning
Instruction given (medication administration): Give the missed dose now with food, take tomorrow's dose in the morning as usual, and never double up or stop it suddenly
Instruction given (symptom monitoring): Steroids can cause restlessness and a big appetite; give it in the morning and watch for stomach pain or black stools
Reason for call: Wants to understand when to use each medicine in the comfort kit delivered today (The kit was delivered this afternoon; she is not symptomatic right now)
Medication: morphine, 20 mg/mL, 0.25 mL, under the tongue, every 2 hours, as needed, status: prescribed
Medication: lorazepam, 0.5 mg, under the tongue, every 4 hours, as needed, status: prescribed
Medication: haloperidol, 0.5 mg, every 6 hours, as needed, status: prescribed
Medication: atropine, 1 percent drops, 2 drops, under the tongue, every 4 hours, as needed, status: prescribed
Pertinent negative: pain or breathing difficulty right now, She is sleeping comfortably
Symptom present: sleeping more, sleeps most of the day, this week
Background: Afraid of giving the wrong medicine or too much
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, tomorrow at 11, because review the kit and demonstrate giving each medicine
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, morphine, because pain or shortness of breath
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, lorazepam, because anxiety or restlessness
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, haloperidol, because agitation or confusion or nausea
Nurse action (advised): medication instruction, atropine, because noisy or wet breathing
Instruction given (medication administration): Use the syringe that came with the bottle, place it between the cheek and gum, write down every dose and time
Instruction given (callback invitation): Call before giving if unsure which one to use, any time day or night
Instruction given (safety): Keep the kit in one spot away from children and pets and keep the hospice phone number on the box
Reason for call: Gave the weekly update on his daughter's tracheostomy and asked about swimming (Pediatric home care patient with a tracheostomy)
Symptom present: thin white secretions, mild
Supply: suction catheters, 3 catheters remaining
Supply: spare trach tubes, 1 tubes remaining
Pertinent negative: fever or trouble breathing
Background: She started preschool two days a week with a nurse aide
Nurse action (planned): message to team, pulmonologist, because question about swimming with a tracheostomy
Nurse action (planned): nurse visit, Friday
Nurse action (planned): supply order, suction catheters and a spare trach tube
Instruction given (equipment use): Keep two spare tubes of her size and one smaller size with her at all times, change the tube on schedule, and keep the humidifier running
